title: Purchasing & Supplier Intelligence
subtitle: What you bought, from whom, at what price, and whether that price is moving.

relationship.subtitle: Purchase spend against the cost of what actually sold, over the same period.
relationship.balanced: Buying roughly in step with sales
relationship.unavailable: Nothing sold in this period, so there is no cost to compare against.
relationship.note: Above 1 means stock is building up; below 1 means it is being drawn down.

concentration.subtitle: How much of the spend rests on how few suppliers.
concentration.hhiHint: Sum of squared shares. 1.00 is a single supplier; 0.10 is about ten equal ones.
concentration.unavailable: Fewer than two suppliers bought from in this period, so there is nothing to concentrate.

breakdown.subtitle: Attributed from purchase lines, so it will not match the spend total exactly when line and header disagree.

suppliers.subtitle: Spend is per purchase order; units and products come from the lines.
suppliers.empty: No supplier was bought from in this period.

products.subtitle: Unit cost is quantity-weighted. A price change is only shown when both periods have units.
products.empty: No product was purchased in this period.

highlights.title: What to look at
highlights.empty: Nothing needs attention in this period.
highlights.spendUp: Purchase spend rose {{changePercent}} against the comparison period.
highlights.spendDown: Purchase spend fell {{changePercent}} against the comparison period.
highlights.stockBuilding: You spent {{ratio}} times what sold cost. Stock is building up.
highlights.stockDrawdown: You spent well below what sold cost. Stock is being drawn down.
highlights.concentration: {{sharePercent}} of spend went to a single supplier.
highlights.unpaid: {{amountValue}} of this period's purchases is still unpaid.
highlights.supplierReturns: {{units}} units were raised back to suppliers.
highlights.resumed: Purchasing restarted after a period with none.

basis.title: How these figures are built
basis.spend: Spend comes from the purchase total — what was owed to the supplier.
basis.attribution: Anything per product, category or brand comes from the purchase lines, because a purchase total cannot be attributed to a single product.

states.empty: There were no purchases in this period.
states.emptyHint: Try a longer period, or clear the filters.
states.error: The purchasing report could not be loaded.
states.forbidden: You do not have access to reports.

restricted: Purchase costs are hidden because this account does not hold the cost permission. Quantities and supplier activity are unaffected.
